videos.script: A Go program is one file to copy. Until it needs a page, a template or a banner from the disk. This lesson puts those inside the binary. {{one}} First, one file into one variable, with a comment the go command reads. Change the file after the build and the program does not notice. It copied the contents when it was built. {{missing}} A missing file is a build error, not an empty string. So is a directive in a file that forgot to import embed. {{tree}} Then a whole directory, as a file system inside the program. Files whose names start with a dot or an underscore stay out unless you ask, and that is a safety measure. {{serve}} Last, a web server that carries its own pages. You delete the directory it was built from, and it goes on serving. {{close}} Lesson 25 starts the last part of the course: testing, with a package you build over six lessons.
